details: Scan a configurable root for .lattices.json, list configured projects, and show their panes and running session status.
caveat: Discovery scans up to three levels and skips .git and node_modules.

details: Detect Bun, pnpm, Yarn, or npm and select dev, start, serve, or watch from package.json.
caveat: CLI and app have different package-manager precedence if multiple lockfiles exist.

details: Identify each project session by its directory basename and six hexadecimal SHA-256 characters from the absolute path.
caveat: Renaming or moving a project changes its session identity.

details: Declare pane names, commands and first-pane width; build a two-pane split or a main pane with supporting panes.
caveat: Requires tmux. With no detected dev command and no configured panes, the default is a single shell.

details: Create or reconnect to a project session; launch, attach, detach, list or kill sessions through CLI and native controls.
caveat: Requires tmux. Sessions survive terminal closure or disconnection; reboot survival is not implemented by ordinary tmux creation.

details: On reattach, rerun exited commands automatically with ensure, or type them into idle panes for manual submission with prefill.
caveat: Requires tmux and an idle pane recognized as a shell. Ensure takes precedence when both flags are enabled.

details: Recreate missing panes, restore pane labels and restart declared commands in idle panes.
caveat: Requires tmux. Layout is reapplied when missing panes are recreated; this is not a continuous background reconciler.

details: Restart a pane command by name or index, first interrupting it and escalating if it remains running.
caveat: Requires tmux. Restart can terminate child processes; a pane without a declared command is left at its shell.

details: Launch work in Terminal, iTerm2, Warp, Ghostty, Kitty or Alacritty, choosing among installed terminals.
caveat: Terminal and iTerm2 have specific focus/attach scripting; other terminals use app activation on this path.

details: Detect Node, Swift, Rust, Go, Make or the Lattices hybrid project and run or build it with lats dev.
caveat: The corresponding toolchain must be installed. Non-Lattices restart delegates to build rather than restarting an arbitrary service.

details: Group terminal projects and application windows; match app titles, open missing URLs or apps, and select tabs by label or index.
caveat: Configured groups persist in workspace.json; terminal project members require tmux.

details: Create a group from selected existing windows, focus its members, split them side by side, collapse them or ungroup them.
caveat: Live stacks are runtime-only. Hiding floating controls does not delete the group.

details: Gather project and app windows into named layers; switch context, explicitly apply tiles, or launch missing members.
caveat: Current configuration is ~/.lattices/workspace.json. Switching, tiling and launching are distinct operations.

details: Match app names, titles and sessions with exact, substring or regular-expression criteria, plus Space, visibility and exclusions.
caveat: Every field inside a clause must match. The retired ~/.lattices/layers.json file is no longer read.

details: Add a window to a layer, pin it across title changes, remove eligible single-window entries, or move it between layers.
caveat: A broad entry that also matches other windows can prevent removing only one member; edit the rule instead.

details: Resolve each content window to at most one layer using pin, matching rule, group, project, then app/title precedence.
caveat: Configured entries and live matching windows are separate states. Saved pins have explicit close/rebind semantics.

details: Arrange layer windows with Auto, Columns or Master-stack; adapt Auto to standard and ultrawide displays.
caveat: Automatic layout acts on the main display's current desktop. Explicit tile or display entries keep their assigned place.

details: Hide unused apps, park other windows of shared apps, and restore a layer's additional scene windows when returning.
caveat: Operates on the main display and current desktop. Some apps refuse off-screen parking; other displays and desktops stay in place.

details: Restore parked frames and apps hidden by layer switches, including saved parking recovery after an app crash.
caveat: Windows on another desktop may need that desktop to be shown before restoration. Apps hidden independently by the user stay hidden.

details: Switch using eight direct slots around a 3×3 pad or directional arrows; use the center slot to show the current layer.
caveat: Eight is the direct shortcut capacity, not a demonstrated hard maximum on saved layer count.

details: Create, rename or delete layers; add, replace or remove entries; change layout while maintaining active-layer selection.
caveat: Saved configuration changes take effect through the documented switch or explicit rearrangement actions.

details: See scaled monitor maps and their desktops, with a tray for windows the maps cannot place and an on-demand working list.
caveat: Current working-source implementation, including uncommitted changes; release and installed-app behavior were not reverified in this audit.

details: Browse by layer, monitor, desktop, window kind or search, and select or extend a window selection without rearranging the desktop.
caveat: Choosing a layer in Overview scopes inspection; it does not activate that layer.

details: Distinguish live, last-known and saved-home positions, and show whether a window is visible, elsewhere, full screen, hidden, parked or unlocated.
caveat: Unknown placement is labeled rather than invented. Saved configuration does not prove a currently open matching window.

details: Focus or place one window, carry it to another desktop on its monitor, or tile, distribute and arrange a selected group per monitor.
caveat: Only eligible windows are moved; excluded windows remain selected and untouched. Individual placement requires the monitor's current desktop.

details: Edit a layer's layout and tucked windows, save configuration alone, or save and rearrange the active layer.
caveat: Save and rearrange is offered only for the active layer; failed saving prevents rearrangement.

details: Find windows, applications, configured projects, sessions, layers, groups and actions from a shared search surface.
caveat: Search results depend on the available inventory. The default daemon search excludes OCR unless explicitly requested.

details: Search titles, apps, sessions, working directories, terminal tabs, tmux metadata, processes and indexed OCR with explicit source selection.
caveat: --deep and --all request every source. Terminal inspection and OCR availability depend on the relevant app support and permissions.

details: Filter search by time and recency, return JSON or window IDs, and report matched sources and terminal details.
caveat: Results refer to the observed inventory and can become stale before a later mutation.

details: Draw a proportional terminal floor plan or versioned JSON projection, preserving monitor topology, window geometry and per-display front-to-back order.
caveat: Current-Space windows only. Prefers desktop.snapshot and falls back on older builds; this opens no visible Lattices UI.

details: Move one or several selected windows to the next or a named monitor while keeping normalized frames, or move and place one in a specific slot.
caveat: Requires available display topology and Accessibility. Move-and-place is intentionally omitted for multi-selection to avoid stacking it into one slot.

details: Focus a project's terminal across Spaces, using window tags and available native fallback paths, and switch adjacent Spaces with instant navigation.
caveat: Permission-dependent. Instant switching temporarily overrides the corresponding Mission Control hotkeys and restores them when disabled or on quit.

details: Select real windows, fill open space, grid a selection, swap two windows or stage a placement; keep changes or restore the original arrangement.
caveat: Fill, Grid and Swap act immediately; Place is staged. Restore returns frames and stacking to the opening state. Requires window-control permissions.

details: Open a searchable palette for project/session, group, layer, tiling and application commands; bare lats shows status without attaching.
caveat: tmux-specific actions require tmux; native window operations require the running app.

details: Keep project pane configuration in .lattices.json and layer/group declarations in ~/.lattices/workspace.json, refreshed by the app.
caveat: This provides declarative configuration; a dedicated reusable template catalog and Git-management interface were not found in the audited core.
